title: A film no device can play as it is is re-encoded, and an HDR film looks right on an ordinary screen
description: Serves PRODUCT.md: "Only when nothing else works is the picture re-encoded, and an HDR film then looks right on an ordinary screen", "No codec, HDR format or subtitle kind is second-class" and "Play starts in seconds and keeps up." The engine's re-encode, tone mapping and sharing of slow films across workers are carried over here.
acceptanceCriteria: A film whose picture the device can't play is re-encoded to one it plays; HDR10, HDR10+, HLG and Dolby Vision films, profile 5 included, look right on an ordinary screen, observed on a real player.

A film one worker can't make as fast as it is watched is shared across workers, so it keeps up; a viewer waiting for a worker takes room from that sharing at most once and only as much as it needs, and sharing starts as soon as there is room.
When the cluster can't make a film as fast as it is watched, the viewer is told why at Play, or before the picture would freeze, never left with a frozen picture.
Checking whether a piece of a film is already made reads none of it; the object-storage traffic of one film made slower than real time is measured and stated.
A seek anywhere gives the right picture and sound from its first frame.
Proven on Media3 on Android TV and phone emulators and on hls.js in Chromium; the design states the CPU and storage one re-encoded playback costs.
notes: Lighter picture steps and following the connection are stage 3 (JS-322); until then a re-encode makes one quality.
